newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Supreme Court rejects Virginia redistricting.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Supreme Court rejects Virginia redistricting.

text.p: The Supreme Court on Friday affirmed a ruling that struck down as unconstitutional Virginia's only majority-black congressional district.
The justices rejected appeals by Virginia Republican Attorney General James Gilmore and by civil rights groups arguing that the redistricting plan should be upheld.
At issue was Virginia's Third Congressional District, which is 64 percent black and stretches about 225 miles from Richmond to Hampton Roads.

Democrat Robert Scott of Newport News was elected from the district in 1992, becoming the first black member of Congress from Virginia since the Reconstruction-era after the Civil War. He won re-election in 1994 and 1996.
The three-judge federal court panel struck down the district, created in 1991 by the Democratic-controlled legislature, on the grounds that race had been the main factor in drawing the boundaires.
The judges ordered the Virginia legislature to redraw the boundaries before the 1998 elections.
